To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) meadow stepp grasslands in the Western Siberia are highly diverse and (ii) species-rich meadow stepp vegetation is maintained in small remnants in forest-grasslands mosaics and (iii) species-poor vegetation is maintained in large meadow stepp remnants with low grazing pressure.
the species richness in meadow steppes was higher in communities with lower soil salinity and lower soil moisture, and in forest-grass- land mosaics.
meadow steppe plant species richness and functional structure are affected by local and landscape factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of the remaining meadow steppe remnants, which are of high value for biodiversity in agricultural landscapes.
the effects of past and present management on plant diversity and provides a baseline for conservation and restoration of meadow steppes in agricultural landscape of the Western Siberian plain.
the conservation of biodiversity in grasslands of the Western Siberian plain and provides important information for the management of meadow steppes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meadow steppe of the Western Siberian plain has suffered from severe degradation in the last 50-100 years.
the current state of meadow stepps is in a critical state, with a high probability of further decline.
the current condition of meadow steeps is very bad.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the meadow steppe vegetation in the study area is still highly threatened by habitat loss and degradation, and that a large part of the current species richness in meadow steppes is likely a remnant of the former extent and diversity of meadow steppes in this region.

the present state of meadow stepes in the Western Sibirian plain is a result of the past land-use history and that the current land-use and landscape structure is the major determinant of the floristic diversity patterns.
the conservation of meadow stepe communities is a challenging task, which needs to consider both local and landscape factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conservation of meadow steppes in the Western Siberia requires a combination of landscape and local scale management measures.
meadow stepps have been severely degraded and are now threatened by extinction debt.
the conservation of meadow steppes requires the restoration of the mosaic structure of the landscape and the implementation of low-intensity management practices.
